Alex 
 great to meet you. Appreciated the context and the assets. Short answers + proposed next steps below.

Recommended models to evaluate (fast path):
- redwood-rlhf-13b-v2 (best balance of output fidelity and cost for structured JSON)
- redwood-8b-q4f (quantized profile for lower cost; expect ~10-15% latency improvement, watch for subtle tokenization edge cases)
- redwood-70b-p8-std (higher-cost variant if you need strict schema fidelity at scale)

Benchmarks / evals:
- I uploaded a targeted eval for your prompt set here: https://app.redwood.ai/evals/avery-2027-04 (you'll see result CSV attached: redwood-eval-results.csv). The summary shows the 13b model hits schema-compliance ~92% on your current prompt set; 8b-q4f is ~86% but with lower cost.

Structured-output / JSON schema:
- We ran structured-output evals against the schema you shared (a couple of the prompts produced missing fields). For schema enforcement we recommend a two-layer approach: 1) model-level validation with strict schema prompts + canonicalization; 2) runtime validation & deterministic retries for tool calls that return invalid JSON.
- Typical retry policy we recommend: up to 2 automatic retries with a small temperature/penalty tweak, then fallback to a stable model variant (redwood-70b-p8-std) if schema still fails.

Attachments: redwood-eval-results.csv (summary), a suggested prompt tuning checklist, and the prompt sets you sent (avery-prompt-sets.jsonl).

Proposed mutual action plan (high level):
1) This week: Redwood sends recommended eval configs + updated prompt-set with schema guard variants (we've attached an initial pass).
2) Avery runs the evals (we provide test harness + instructions).
3) Week 2: Review results, pick pilot model variant and quantization profile; agree SLOs for schema compliance and latency.
4) Pilot: 2-4 week test with canary routing and regression monitoring via Redwood Console.

Next steps: Aditya, can you add a runbook for the structured-output eval + the GitHub runner link? Rishi, please confirm recommended quantization profile and any infra caveats. Alex

Thanks Marissa 
 linking the runner and a couple of concrete infra notes here.

Runner / tools: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-runner (readme has the Avery eval example). We'll drop a pre-built job file in the shared Drive folder.

Technical notes on retries & JSON compliance:
- Retry strategy: 2 automatic attempts with temperature set to 0.0 and an instruction to strictly follow the schema. If still invalid, record a failure and route to fallback model variant. We recommend recording the raw model outputs + the normalized parse result in the eval CSV for auditability.
- Enforcement: use model-assisted canonicalizers (lightweight Code-LLM pass) that attempt to correct JSON minor issues (trailing commas, single quotes). We treat corrections as best-effort and still count toward schema compliance metrics; corrected vs native outputs are both tracked.
- Tool/function calling specific: tag tool calls with an idempotency token (request_id) so retries are safe on the receiver side. For side-effecting actions, prefer to do a dry-run first in pilot.

Quantization / infer infra: redwood-8b-q4f works well for throughput; if you need more determinism, redwood-rlhf-13b-v2 at fp16 (p8) gives much higher schema fidelity. We'll include kernel/latency profiles in the run artifact.

I'll put the eval job and S3 staging instructions in the Drive link and add a short runbook snippet to the HubSpot record.
